subject: Information Theory
title: ASCII and Unicode
description: A quick win: understand ASCII and Unicode.

hook.text: ASCII fit every English character into 7 bits. Then the rest of the world's languages needed a seat at the table.

buildup.text: ASCII assigned numbers 0–127 to letters, digits, and control characters. Simple, fast, but English-only.

discovery.text: Unicode expanded to 149,000+ characters: every modern script, historical scripts, and yes—emoji.

twist.text: UTF-8 encodes Unicode as variable-length bytes. ASCII stays one byte; rare characters use up to four.

climax.text: UTF-8 dominates the web. It's backward-compatible with ASCII and handles every language efficiently.

punchline.text: From 128 characters to 149,000. UTF-8 bridged the gap.

quiz.question: Why is UTF-8 widely adopted?
options: It's backward-compatible with ASCII and handles all languages
